drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Thank you. We propose the attached Cause definition and a narrower, conditional non-compete with express exceptions. The non-compete remains subject to review under the governing law and the Executive’s actual work location; we do not assume that a twelve-month restriction is enforceable.

Other substantive points requiring resolution are termination procedures, any Good Reason protection, accrued compensation, severance conditions and payment timing, bonus and equity treatment, benefits, confidentiality and intellectual property, indemnification and D&O coverage, and dispute resolution. Please also confirm the reporting line and whether employment is at will or for a specified term. The draft comments flag these issues now so that they can be addressed alongside the missing particulars.

All proposed language and outstanding commercial terms remain subject to express client approval. No agreement on compensation, severance or restrictive covenants should be inferred.

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE AND CAUSE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, the Executive shall receive the Severance Amount, with the amount or formula, payment schedule, benefits treatment and any conditions to be expressly agreed in this Agreement. “Cause” means: (a) fraud, embezzlement or intentional misappropriation by the Executive involving the Company; (b) conviction of, or a plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving fraud or dishonesty that materially impairs the Executive’s ability to perform the role; (c) willful misconduct in performing the Executive’s duties that causes material harm to the Company; or (d) a material breach of this Agreement or willful and continued failure to perform material duties consistent with the Executive’s position and lawful written directions, other than because of illness or incapacity. An act or omission is not willful if undertaken in good faith with a reasonable belief that it was in the Company’s best interests. Failure to meet performance targets alone does not constitute Cause. Before terminating for Cause, the Company shall provide written notice stating the specific grounds and a reasonable opportunity for the Executive to respond to the Board. For grounds capable of cure, the Executive shall have thirty days after notice to cure; timely cure precludes termination for Cause on those grounds. A Cause determination must be made in good faith by the Board, excluding the Executive if a director, following that process. Earned but unpaid salary, properly reimbursable expenses and other accrued entitlements required by applicable law or governing benefit plans shall be paid regardless of the reason for termination and shall not be conditioned on a release.

4. PROPOSED NON-COMPETE—SUBJECT TO APPLICABLE-LAW REVIEW AND EXPRESS AGREEMENT. No post-employment non-compete shall apply unless the parties expressly agree in the executed Agreement on the restricted business, territory, duration and any legally required consideration. Any agreed restriction shall apply only to the extent permitted by the law applicable to the Executive, including mandatory law of the Executive’s work location. The proposed restriction would prohibit only duties substantially similar to those actually performed by the Executive during the final twelve months of employment for a business directly competing with specifically identified Company products or services for which the Executive had material responsibility. Its territory would be limited to specifically identified markets in which the Executive had material responsibility during that period, and its duration would not exceed twelve months, without automatic extension or tolling. It would not prohibit: (a) passive ownership of up to two percent of the outstanding securities of a publicly traded company, without management participation; (b) work for a separately operated, non-competing division of a diversified business, provided the Executive does not provide services to its competing business; (c) activities outside the expressly defined restricted business or territory; or (d) activities approved by the Company in writing. The proposed restriction would not apply following termination by the Company without Cause or resignation for Good Reason, if Good Reason protection is agreed. Nothing in this section restricts lawful reporting to regulators, protected disclosures, cooperation with government investigations, or other legally protected activity.

Please specify reporting line, principal duties, work location, travel expectations, effective date and whether employment is at will or for a specified term. We reserve review of any exclusivity requirement and propose exceptions for approved outside activities that do not materially interfere with duties or create a conflict.

In addition to the missing compensation particulars, please address bonus eligibility and payment on termination, equity vesting and post-termination exercise rights, benefit-plan participation, expense reimbursement and any proposed clawback. Identify any incorporated plans or policies and provide them for review.

Please address notice and termination mechanics, death and disability, and whether severance also applies to resignation for Good Reason. Proposed Good Reason triggers for discussion are a material reduction in base salary, material diminution of duties or authority, material required relocation, or material Company breach, with agreed notice and cure procedures. Any release condition, payment deadline, tax-compliance provision, offset, mitigation obligation or cessation of severance requires express agreement; none should be implied.

Please provide the governing law and actual work location before restrictive-covenant language is finalized. The proposed twelve-month ceiling is not agreement that twelve months is necessary or enforceable. Please identify any proposed non-solicitation restriction separately. Other outstanding substantive subjects are appropriately limited confidentiality and IP provisions, including prior-invention and protected-disclosure exceptions; indemnification and D&O coverage; dispute forum and any arbitration terms; assignment; notices; and integration and amendment provisions. Any such provisions remain subject to review and express approval.
